clue.text: Cover rejected — novel is an embarrassment

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word for the cover is read from right to left

parts.note: a lid is a cover
Emma is Jane Austen's novel

explanation.surface: Someone turns down a book jacket, and the novel inside proves a source of shame.
explanation.definitionFit: An embarrassment in the older sense is a perplexing predicament, a fair synonym for an awkward choice between two evils.

clue.text: Fierce woman admits love for bully

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the fierce woman's word takes the love letter inside it

parts.note: a dragon is a fierce, formidable woman
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A formidable woman confesses she loves a bully.
explanation.definitionFit: To dragoon someone is to coerce or browbeat them, a verb synonym for bully.

clue.text: Primrose, say, has abandoned squabbling

parts.note: abandoned in the sense of wanton or unrestrained means loose
squabbling is strife

explanation.surface: A woman called Primrose has given up arguing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primrose' looks like a woman's name; it is the plant family.
explanation.definitionFit: Loosestrife is a plant of the primrose family, so 'say' marks it as an example.

clue.text: It flowers a short time in Siam wild

indicators.note: the short-time word sits inside the rearranged letters
wild suggests disorder, so the letters of Siam are jumbled

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a short time

explanation.surface: Some plant blooms for only a brief spell in the Thai wilderness.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimosa is a flowering shrub, so it is a thing that flowers.

clue.text: Versatile sportsman takes part in the whole game without quarter

parts.note: the whole means all

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter is taken out of the game

parts.note: rounders is a British bat-and-ball game, rather like baseball
a quarter is a compass point, here S for south

explanation.surface: An all-round player joins in a full match without giving any mercy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops S from ROUNDERS; 'takes part in' is linking padding. 'without quarter' reads as 'without mercy'.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-rounder is a player skilled at several aspects of a sport, especially cricket.

clue.text: Terrorists' leader organised squat in passage

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: to run something is to organise it, past tense ran
to squat is to sit

explanation.surface: A terrorist chief arranged a squat in some corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit is passage from one place to another, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Lock keeper finally leaving Hardy's pure woman

indicators.note: a letter leaving the word is removed from it

parts.note: a lock of hair is a tress

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of keeper

explanation.surface: A lock-keeper finally departs from Thomas Hardy's heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes R from 'keeper'; 'leaving' removes it from TRESS. 'Lock keeper' reads as a canal job.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Hardy's novel Tess of the d'Urbervilles is subtitled 'A Pure Woman'.

clue.text: Hate a man falsifying a denunciation

indicators.note: falsifying means distorting, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man is lying about his hatred.
explanation.definitionFit: An anathema is a formal curse or denunciation, especially by the church.

clue.text: Support under a jumper

parts.note: a jumper reads as a sweater, but here it is a ... jumper standing on the support beneath

explanation.definitionFit: A ski is the runner beneath a ski jumper's feet that supports them.

clue.text: It attached Alpine climbers to their supports

definitions.text: It attached Alpine climbers to their supports

parts.words: It attached Alpine climbers to their supports
parts.note: reads as a mountaineer's rope, but the climbers are plants on mountains clinging with fine coils

explanation.definitionFit: A tendril is the thread-like organ by which a climbing plant clings to a support.

clue.text: The year that doesn't exist spells trouble

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, labels a year
nothing, the figure zero, read as the letter O

explanation.surface: A missing year in the calendar is bound to cause problems.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no year AD 0 in the calendar, which jumps from 1 BC to AD 1.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado means fuss or bother, a synonym for trouble.

clue.text: Bugging spy headquarters

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation
a station is a base or headquarters

explanation.surface: Secret listening devices are planted at an intelligence agency's main office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bugging' suggests surveillance; it is the sense of pestering.
explanation.definitionFit: Bugging in the sense of pestering or harassing is a form of molestation.

clue.text: Bowling dangerous: needed to pull back?

parts.note: in cricket, bowling is delivered in overs of six balls
hot means dangerous, as in a hot situation

explanation.surface: Hostile fast bowling in cricket forces the batsman to retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: Having overshot a target, one has gone too far and needs to come back, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Drink for one in the national hunt

definitions.meaning: a short drink taken straight after another, such as whisky after beer
a horse that races over fences in National Hunt racing, the British jumps season

explanation.definitionFit: A chaser is a drink taken after another, and also a steeplechase horse in National Hunt racing.

clue.text: Upright journeyman who needs to get a grip

definitions.text: Upright journeyman who needs to get a grip

parts.words: Upright journeyman who needs to get a grip
parts.note: not a craftsman but a standing commuter on a bus or train holding the overhead loop

explanation.definitionFit: A straphanger is a standing passenger who holds a strap on public transport.

clue.text: Philosopher involved in publicity work for the liturgy

indicators.note: the philosopher's name is caught up inside the other pieces

parts.note: PR is public relations, publicity
a book is a written work
A. J. Ayer was a British philosopher

explanation.surface: A thinker gets into advertising work to promote church services.
explanation.definitionFit: A prayer book contains the set forms of public worship, the liturgy.

clue.text: Security agreement accepted by senator

indicators.note: taken in by the word, so the answer is found within its letters

explanation.surface: A senator approves a defence treaty.
explanation.definitionFit: NATO is the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation, a collective security alliance.

clue.text: Ultramarine endlessly analysed as part of normal university studies

definitions.text: as part of normal university studies

indicators.note: analysed means broken down into parts, so the letters are rearranged
without its end, so the last letter of the colour word goes

explanation.surface: A blue pigment is studied endlessly in an ordinary college course.
explanation.definitionFit: Intramural means within the walls of an institution, so applied to studies inside one university.

clue.text: Railings round painting in gym

parts.note: pales are fence stakes, railings

indicators.note: turning round reverses the word for painting

parts.note: painting is art

explanation.surface: A painting hangs surrounded by railings in a gymnasium.
explanation.definitionFit: A palaestra was a wrestling school or gymnasium in ancient Greece.

clue.text: Soldier has to look warily at investigator

parts.note: a private is a soldier of the lowest rank
to eye is to look at warily

explanation.surface: A soldier must keep a wary watch on a detective.
explanation.definitionFit: A private eye is a private detective, an investigator for hire.

clue.text: Anaemic child needs a coat

parts.note: anaemic people look pale
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A sickly-looking youngster needs a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A paletot is a loose outer coat or overcoat.

clue.text: Whichever way you move, it's mate

indicators.note: reading in either direction gives the same letters

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Some chess move always ends in checkmate.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppo is British slang for a colleague or friend, a mate.

clue.text: Young person thus bound is not allowed to draw back

parts.note: out means not permitted, as in 'smoking is out'

indicators.note: drawing back reverses the word draw

explanation.surface: A youngster heading off may not back out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DRAW to WARD. 'Young person' looks like WARD alone, but the definition plays on Outward Bound, the outdoor adventure school.
explanation.definitionFit: Outward Bound is a youth adventure-training scheme, so a youngster on it is bound in this way.

clue.text: The way the Navy gets up to date

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Navy procedures get updated.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern means current, up to date.

clue.text: Regularly agrees to pursue untruth in Lords

indicators.note: the following piece chases the other, so it comes after

parts.note: a lie is an untruth

indicators.note: every other letter of agrees is taken

explanation.surface: Peers routinely accept chasing a falsehood in the House of Lords.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieges are feudal lords to whom allegiance is owed.

clue.text: Classical sailor bearing gold, in the vernacular

indicators.note: the bearing and gold letters go inside the slang word

parts.note: argot is slang, everyday vernacular speech
a compass bearing such as N for north
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: An ancient seaman carries gold and speaks in slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argonauts sailed with Jason on the Argo in Greek legend.

clue.text: Detached place in Surrey looks expensive from the front

indicators.note: the front letters of each word are taken

explanation.surface: A secluded home in Surrey looks pricey from the street.
explanation.definitionFit: An isle is a piece of land detached from the mainland.

clue.text: Shorebird about to be fossilised

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the bird's name is wrapped round the other word

parts.note: a turnstone is a wading bird of the shore

explanation.surface: A coastal bird is on the point of becoming a fossil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shorebird about to' reads as a bird on the point of doing something; 'about' is really the signal for one word wrapping another.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn to stone is to petrify, as in fossilisation.

clue.text: Wide ladder

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a wide is a ball out of reach that gives the batting side an extra
a ladder is a line of unravelled stitches in stockings

explanation.definitionFit: A wide in cricket scores an extra run, and a ladder in tights is a run.

clue.text: Visit a part of subcontinent

parts.note: to go to a place is to visit it

explanation.surface: Pay a visit to a region of India.
explanation.definitionFit: Goa is a state on India's west coast, part of the Indian subcontinent.

clue.text: In general character, complainant carried weight

indicators.note: carried means held within, so the complainer goes inside

parts.note: tone is the general character of something
a nag is a persistent complainer

explanation.surface: Broadly speaking, the complainer had real influence.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonnage is the weight or carrying capacity of a ship, measured in tons.

clue.text: Having qualities similar to a pleasant claret

parts.note: kind means pleasant, friendly
claret is red wine, or the colour red

explanation.surface: Something resembles a nice red Bordeaux.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindred as an adjective means similar in nature, like kindred spirits.
